questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II
List-I
a) A matrix which is not a square matrix
b) A square matrix $A'=A$
c) The diagonal elements of a diagonal matrix are same
d) A matrix which is both symmetric and skew symmetric
List-II
i) Symmetric matrix
ii) Null matrix
iii) Rectangular matrix
iv) Scalar matrix
Codes:
options: a - iii, b - i, c - iv, d - ii
a - iii, b - ii, c - iv, d - i
a - i, b - ii, c - iv, d - iii
a - iii, b - iv, c - i, d - ii
questions.note: The correct match is a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii (option A); KEA's key credits option (3) (a-i, b-ii, c-iv, d-iii), which misassigns 'a' and 'b'.
questions.explanation: a is a rectangular matrix (iii), b is a symmetric matrix (i), c is a scalar matrix (iv), and d (symmetric and skew-symmetric together) must be the null matrix (ii), giving a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii; KEA's key marks option (3) as correct (as per KEA key).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I : If $A$ is a non-singular matrix, then $A^{-1}$ exists.
Statement II : If $A$ and $B$ are symmetric matrices of same order, then $(AB-BA)$ is a skew symmetric matrix.
Choose the correct option.
options: Statement I is true and Statement II is false
Statement I is false and Statement II is false
Statement I is true and Statement II is true
Statement I is false and Statement II is true
questions.explanation: A non-singular matrix always has an inverse (Statement I true). For symmetric $A,B$: $(AB-BA)'=B'A'-A'B'=BA-AB=-(AB-BA)$, so it is skew symmetric (Statement II true).

questions.q: A row matrix has only
options: One row with one or more columns
One column with one or more rows
questions.explanation: By definition, a row matrix has exactly one row and one or more columns.

questions.q: Let $X$ be a matrix of order $2\times n$ and $Z$ be a matrix of order $2\times p$. If $n=p$, then the order of the matrix $7X-5Z$ is:
questions.explanation: Since $n=p$, both matrices have order $2\times n$, and subtraction/addition preserves order, so $7X-5Z$ is $2\times n$.

questions.q: If A is a square matrix such that $A^2=A$, then $(I-A)^3$ is
questions.explanation: $(I-A)^2=I-2A+A^2=I-A$, which is idempotent, so $(I-A)^3=(I-A)(I-A)^2=(I-A)(I-A)=I-A$.

questions.q: If A and B are two matrices such that AB is an identity matrix and the order of matrix B is 3 × 4, then the order of matrix A is
questions.explanation: For AB to be a square identity matrix with B being 3×4, A must be 4×3 so that AB is 4×4.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is not correct?
options: A row matrix has only one row
A diagonal matrix has all diagonal elements equal to zero
A symmetric matrix A is a square matrix satisfying A' = A.
A skew symmetric matrix has all diagonal elements equal to zero
questions.explanation: A diagonal matrix has all off-diagonal elements zero (the diagonal entries can be anything), so option (2) is incorrect.

questions.q: If a matrix $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{bmatrix}$ satisfies $A^6=kA'$, then the value of k is
questions.explanation: A is symmetric with $A^2=2A$, so $A^n=2^{n-1}A$; $A^6=32A=32A'$, giving k = 32.

questions.q: If A is a square matrix satisfying the equation $A^2-5A+7I=0$, where I is the identity matrix and 0 is null matrix of same order, then $A^{-1}=$
questions.explanation: Multiplying $A^2-5A+7I=0$ by $A^{-1}$: $A-5I+7A^{-1}=0 \Rightarrow A^{-1}=\dfrac{1}{7}(5I-A)$.

questions.q: If A is square matrix such that $A^2=A$, then $(I+A)^3$ is equal to
questions.explanation: $(I+A)^3=I+3A+3A^2+A^3$. Since $A^2=A$ (and hence $A^3=A$), this equals $I+3A+3A+A=I+7A$.

questions.q: If $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$, then $A^{10}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: $A^2=2A$, so by induction $A^n=2^{n-1}A$. Hence $A^{10}=2^9A$.

questions.q: If $x\begin{bmatrix}3\\2\end{bmatrix} + y\begin{bmatrix}1\\-1\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}15\\5\end{bmatrix}$ then the value of x and y are
questions.explanation: $3x+y=15$ and $2x-y=5$. Adding: $5x=20 \Rightarrow x=4$, then $y=15-12=3$.

questions.q: If A and B are two matrices such that $AB = B$ and $BA = A$ then $A^2 + B^2 =$
questions.explanation: $A^2 = A(BA) = (AB)A = BA = A$, and similarly $B^2 = B(AB) = (BA)B = AB = B$. So $A^2+B^2 = A+B$.

questions.q: If $A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & \tan(\alpha/2)\\-\tan(\alpha/2) & 1\end{bmatrix}$ and $AB = I$ then $B =$
questions.explanation: $AA^T = \sec^2(\alpha/2) I$, so $A^{-1} = \cos^2(\alpha/2) A^T$; since $AB=I$, $B = A^{-1} = \cos^2(\alpha/2) A^T$.

questions.q: If A = $\begin{bmatrix}0 & 1\\0 & 0\end{bmatrix}$ then (aI + bA)$^n$ is (where I is the identity matrix of order 2)
questions.explanation: Since $A^2=0$, the binomial expansion of $(aI+bA)^n$ truncates after the linear term: $a^nI + na^{n-1}bA$.

questions.q: If A is a matrix of order 3 × 3, then (A$^2$)$^{-1}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: $(A^2)^{-1} = (A^{-1})^2$ by the standard inverse-of-a-power identity.

questions.q: If A = $\begin{bmatrix}2 & -1\\3 & -2\end{bmatrix}$, then the inverse of the matrix A$^3$ is
questions.explanation: Direct computation gives $A^2=I$, so $A^3=A$, and hence $(A^3)^{-1}=A^{-1}=A$ (since here $A^{-1}=A$).

questions.q: If A is a skew symmetric matrix, then A$^{2021}$ is
questions.explanation: For skew symmetric A ($A^T=-A$), odd powers satisfy $(A^n)^T=(-A)^n=-A^n$ for odd n, so $A^{2021}$ is also skew symmetric.

questions.q: If A = $\begin{bmatrix}1 & -2 & 1\\ 2 & 1 & 3\end{bmatrix}$, B = $\begin{bmatrix}2 & 1\\ 3 & 2\\ 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}$ then (AB)' is equal to
questions.explanation: AB = $\begin{bmatrix}-3 & -2\\ 10 & 7\end{bmatrix}$, so its transpose (AB)' = $\begin{bmatrix}-3 & 10\\ -2 & 7\end{bmatrix}$.

questions.q: Let M be 2 $\times$ 2 symmetric matrix with integer entries, then M is invertible if
options: the first column of M is the transpose of second row of M
the second row of M is the transpose of first column of M
M is a diagonal matrix with non-zero entries in the principal diagonal
The product of entries in the principal diagonal of M is the product of entries in the other diagonal
questions.explanation: A diagonal matrix with non-zero diagonal entries has non-zero determinant (product of diagonal entries), so it is always invertible.

questions.q: $A=\begin{pmatrix}0&0&1\\0&1&0\\1&0&0\end{pmatrix}$, then $A^4$ is equal to
questions.explanation: A is a permutation (reflection) matrix with $A^2=I$, so $A^4=(A^2)^2=I$.

questions.q: If A and B are square matrices of same order and B is a skew symmetric matrix, then $A'BA$ is
questions.explanation: $(A'BA)^T = A^T B^T A = -A^T B A = -(A'BA)$, so it is skew symmetric.

questions.q: If $\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\3&2\end{pmatrix}A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$, then the matrix A is
questions.explanation: A is the inverse of $\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\3&2\end{pmatrix}$, whose determinant is $1$, giving $A=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\-3&2\end{pmatrix}$.

questions.q: If P and Q are symmetric matrices of the same order then $PQ-QP$ is
questions.explanation: $(PQ-QP)'=Q'P'-P'Q'=QP-PQ=-(PQ-QP)$, so it is skew-symmetric.

questions.q: If $3A+4B'=\begin{pmatrix}7&-10&17\\0&6&31\end{pmatrix}$ and $2B-3A'=\begin{pmatrix}-1&18\\4&0\\-5&-7\end{pmatrix}$ then $B=$
questions.explanation: Transposing the second equation and adding it to the first eliminates $A$, giving $6B'=\begin{pmatrix}6&-6&12\\18&6&24\end{pmatrix}$, so $B'=\begin{pmatrix}1&-1&2\\3&1&4\end{pmatrix}$ and hence $B$ as in option (A).

questions.q: If $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&3\\4&2\end{pmatrix}, B=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\1&2\end{pmatrix}$, then $|ABB'|=$
If $A=\begin{bmatrix}2 & -2\\ -2 & 2\end{bmatrix}$, then $A^n=2^kA$, where k =
questions.explanation: $A^2=4A$, and by induction $A^n=4^{n-1}A=2^{2(n-1)}A$, so $k=2(n-1)$.

questions.q: If $\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1\\ -1 & 1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x\\ y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2\\ 4\end{bmatrix}$, then the values of x and y respectively are
If $A=\begin{bmatrix}\cos\alpha & \sin\alpha\\ -\sin\alpha & \cos\alpha\end{bmatrix}$, then $AA'=$
questions.explanation: $AA'=\begin{bmatrix}\cos^2\alpha+\sin^2\alpha & 0\\ 0 & \sin^2\alpha+\cos^2\alpha\end{bmatrix}=I$.

questions.q: If $A=\dfrac{1}{\pi}\begin{bmatrix}\sin^{-1}(\pi x) & \tan^{-1}(x/\pi)\\ \sin^{-1}(x/\pi) & \cot^{-1}(\pi x)\end{bmatrix}$, $B=\begin{bmatrix}-\cos^{-1}(\pi x) & \tan^{-1}(x/\pi)\\ \sin^{-1}(x/\pi) & -\tan^{-1}(\pi x)\end{bmatrix}$ then $A-B$ is equal to
questions.explanation: As printed, the entries of B are not scaled by $1/\pi$ like A, making the difference ill-defined, so KEA awarded grace marks to all. Taking the intended matching entries (using $\sin^{-1}\theta+\cos^{-1}\theta=\pi/2$ and $\tan^{-1}\theta+\cot^{-1}\theta=\pi/2$ after scaling by $1/\pi$), $A-B$ works out to the zero matrix (as per KEA key).

questions.q: If a matrix A is both symmetric and skew symmetric, then
questions.explanation: $A=A^T$ and $A=-A^T$ together force $A=-A$, so every entry is 0, i.e. A is the zero matrix.

questions.q: If $2\begin{bmatrix}1&3\\0&x\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}y&0\\1&2\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}5&6\\1&8\end{bmatrix}$, then the value of x and y are
questions.explanation: Comparing entries: $2+y=5\Rightarrow y=3$, and $2x+2=8\Rightarrow x=3$.

questions.q: If A is a matrix of order m \times n and B is a matrix such that AB' and B'A are both defined, the order of the matrix B is
questions.explanation: For $AB'$ to be defined, $B'$ must have $n$ rows; for $B'A$ to be defined, $B'$ must have $m$ columns, so $B'$ is $n\times m$, hence $B$ is $m\times n$.

questions.q: If $A=\begin{bmatrix}\cos2\theta & -\sin2\theta\\ \sin2\theta & \cos2\theta\end{bmatrix}$ and $A + A^T = I$, where I is the unit matrix of $2\times2$ & $A^T$ is the transpose of A, then the value of $\theta$ is equal to
questions.explanation: $A+A^T=\begin{bmatrix}2\cos2\theta&0\\0&2\cos2\theta\end{bmatrix}=I \Rightarrow \cos2\theta=\dfrac12 \Rightarrow \theta=\pi/6$.

questions.q: If $A=\begin{bmatrix}3 & 1\\ -1 & 2\end{bmatrix}$ then $A^2 - 5A$ is equal to
questions.explanation: $A^2=\begin{bmatrix}8&5\\-5&3\end{bmatrix}$ and $5A=\begin{bmatrix}15&5\\-5&10\end{bmatrix}$, so $A^2-5A=\begin{bmatrix}-7&0\\0&-7\end{bmatrix}=-7I$.

questions.q: If $A=\begin{bmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{bmatrix}$, then $A^2$ equal to ____
questions.explanation: $A^2=\begin{bmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{bmatrix}$.

questions.q: If A is 3 $\times$ 4 matrix and B is a matrix such that A'B and BA' are both defined, then B is of the type
questions.explanation: A' is $4\times3$. For A'B to be defined B must have 3 rows; for BA' to be defined B must have 4 columns, so B is $3\times4$.

questions.q: The symmetric part of the matrix A = $\begin{pmatrix}1&2&4\\6&8&2\\2&-2&7\end{pmatrix}$ is
questions.explanation: The symmetric part is $\tfrac12(A+A^T) = \begin{pmatrix}1&4&3\\4&8&0\\3&0&7\end{pmatrix}$.

questions.q: If A and B are square matrices of order 'n' such that $A^2-B^2=(A-B)(A+B)$, then which of the following will be true?
options: Either of A or B is zero matrix.
Either of A or B is an identity matrix.
questions.explanation: Expanding $(A-B)(A+B)=A^2+AB-BA-B^2$ and equating to $A^2-B^2$ gives $AB=BA$.

questions.q: If the matrix $\begin{bmatrix}2&3\\5&-1\end{bmatrix}=A+B$, where A is symmetric and B is skew symmetric, then $B=$
questions.explanation: $B=\dfrac{M-M^T}{2}=\dfrac12\begin{bmatrix}0&-2\\2&0\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{bmatrix}$.

questions.q: If $A=\begin{bmatrix}\cos\theta & \sin\theta\\-\sin\theta & \cos\theta\end{bmatrix}$, then $A\cdot A'$ is ............
questions.explanation: Multiplying $A$ by its transpose gives $\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta=1$ on the diagonal and $0$ off it, i.e. $A\cdot A'=I$.

questions.q: If $A$ and $B$ are symmetric matrices of the same order, then which one of the following is NOT true?
questions.explanation: $(AB-BA)'=B'A'-A'B'=BA-AB=-(AB-BA)$, so $AB-BA$ is skew-symmetric, not symmetric in general.

questions.q: If $A$ and $B$ are two square matrices of the same order such that $AB=B$ and $BA=A$, then $A^2+B^2$ is always equal to
questions.explanation: Since $A=BA$, $A^2=A\cdot A=(AB)A=B(A A)$... more directly $A^2=A(BA)=(AB)A=BA=A$, and similarly $B^2=B(AB)=(BA)B=AB=B$, so $A^2+B^2=A+B$.

questions.q: If $A=\begin{bmatrix}3 & 2\\ 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}$, then $A^2+xA+yI=0$ for $(x, y)=$
questions.explanation: By the Cayley-Hamilton theorem, $A$ satisfies $\lambda^2-(\text{trace})\lambda+|A|=0$, i.e. $A^2-4A+I=0$, so $(x,y)=(-4,1)$.

questions.q: If A and B are square matrices of the same order such that $(A+B)(A-B) = A^2 - B^2$, then $(ABA^{-1})^2 =$
questions.explanation: $(A+B)(A-B)=A^2-B^2$ forces $AB=BA$. Then $(ABA^{-1})^2 = AB(A^{-1}A)BA^{-1} = AB^2A^{-1} = B^2AA^{-1} = B^2$ using $AB=BA$.
